text: We independently review every app we recommend in our best apps lists. When you click some of the links on this page, we may earn a commission. Learn more . Your brand's reputation now lives inside a new algorithm: one that's based on AI searches made in tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. One hallucinated fact, one competitor-favoring answer, and the trust, traffic, and sales can vanish overnight. And with ChatGPT usage soaring and Google's AI answers appearing in nearly half of all searches even on a traditional search engine, the risk (and opportunity) has never been bigger. Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the next generation of SEO, and using LLM visibility tools is essential for understanding how your brand shows up. These tools track where and how your brand appears in AI responses, flag negative sentiment, and spot when competitors start stealing your spotlight. I've researched nearly 50 LLM monitoring tools—and tested as many as I could get my hands on—to deliver the definitive shortlist of proven performers. Beyond surface-level features, I'll dig into each tool's ideal applications so you can pick the one that will help amplify your brand's presence in the AI ecosystem. The best AI visibility tools OtterlyAI for affordability Peec AI for smart suggestions ZipTie for deep analysis and reporting Similarweb for side-by-side SEO and GEO tracking Petra Labs for all-in-one enterprise needs Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit for existing Semrush users Ahrefs Brand Radar for existing Ahrefs users Clearscope for content creators Yext Scout for local tracking What makes the best AI visibility platform? How we evaluate and test apps Our best apps roundups are written by humans who've spent much of their careers using, testing, and writing about software. Unless explicitly stated, we spend dozens of hours researching and testing apps, using each app as it's intended to be used and evaluating it against the criteria we set for the category. We're never paid for placement in our articles from any app or for links to any site—we value the trust readers put in us to offer authentic evaluations of the categories and apps we review. For more details on our process, read the full rundown of how we select apps to feature on the Zapier blog . When I evaluated these LLM monitoring tools, I didn't just skim product pages. I interacted with them as a user and SEO/GEO expert with skin in the game, creating accounts, watching demo videos, booking product walkthroughs, and reading the product documentation. Then, when I was able to get hands-on access, I put each AI search optimization tool through scenarios such as those you'd expect to face as a user: monitoring specific brand mentions, discovering which prompts are driving traffic, and brainstorming what new keywords or prompts a brand might want to be associated with. I tested how they handle different AI search engines, dug into reporting capabilities, and also tested the account setup process. After all that digging, here are the factors I found to be the most important for choosing the best LLM monitoring tool. Just remember: this is such a new software category that no app checks every single box quite yet. Tracking visibility across all AI engines : LLM outputs vary by platform, so you need visibility into how your brand appears across multiple popular generative engines. This ensures you're not blindsided by gaps in one platform, especially those where your customers hang out most. Providing insights and action items : Great LLM visibility tools do more than passively monitor—they interpret what's happening and suggest clear, actionable steps to improve brand positioning. Pay extra attention to platforms that proactively share useful research and best practices. Uncovering trends and patterns : Tracking changes over time helps you spot patterns, whether your brand's visibility is rising, slipping, or reacting to competitor moves—enabling you to respond proactively. Prioritize tools that offer at-a-glance trend oversight. Exploring conversation data (not just the outputs) : Understanding the full context of how users interact with AI engines—including follow-up questions, conversation flow, and the nuanced ways your brand appears throughout multi-turn exchanges—provides deeper insights than simply tracking final outputs. This helps you identify opportunities to appear in related queries and understand the customer journey within AI conversations. Citation source detection : When LLMs cite sources, you want to know which ones. This helps identify high-performing internal pages, potential misinformation sources, and partnership opportunities. Brand visibility scoring (also known as share of voice) : Quantifying how your brand shows up in AI outputs compared to competitors and changes over time helps to measure progress and set concrete goals. Brand sentiment analysis : It's not just about whether you're mentioned, but how . Sentiment analysis helps you track the emotional tone of AI mentions so you can take steps to safeguard brand perception. Competitor benchmarking : Benchmarking against competitors shows whether you're leading, lagging, or keeping pace. AI crawler visibility/technical analysis : This helps you determine if your pages are structured and accessible for AI-driven indexing (and gives you something tangible to focus on if they aren't). Keep in mind that best practices are still being established and constantly changing, but it's good to start somewhere. Integration features : I handed out bonus points for the LLM visibility tools that play nicely with workflow tools like Zapier for seamless automation. It's also worth noting that some tools (like ZipTie) track LLM responses using methods that mimic real user behavior rather than relying solely on APIs. This approach can produce more accurate results since it better reflects what actual users see. There's just a little caveat: LLMs are non-deterministic by nature, meaning the same prompt on the same answer engine at the same time can still produce variations in responses. It's more art than science at this point, so you should expect some fluctuation in the results. Lastly, when choosing a platform, you should factor in your available budget and the value of the offering. In addition to the features mentioned previously, you'll also want to determine the cost per prompt, how it grows in terms of how often you run it, how many AI search engines you're tracking, and the specific geographical regions you're targeting. Hexagons in various colors show your visibility in the corresponding location, so you can know how each of your branches is doing at a glance. Based on this location data, Yext Scout also recommends actions that you can send agents to perform across Yext's marketing tools . These agents do require you to use the rest of the Yext platform, which could be a negative if you're just looking for an AI visibility tool. But if you're willing to go all in on Yext, Scout offers similarly powerful features to other tools on this list. It measures performance against your 20 closest competitors per scan, based on location and trends, so you know which nearby businesses are showing up in AI. Sentiment analysis brings up recurring themes in AI outputs related to your brand, and citation tracking shows which sources those answers use to pinpoint what content to change. As with the rest of the Yext platform, Yext Scout has a very specific user in mind—enterprises with hundreds to thousands of locations. So if you run a handful of sites, your business might be a little too local to get the most out of Yext Scout. Yext Scout pricing: By request; third-party pricing info suggests at least $199/month Which LLM monitoring tool should you choose? Unfortunately, to get everything you want out of an AI visibility tool right now, you may need to use (and pay for) more than one. But even if you're willing to pay top dollar, measuring LLM visibility is still a bit of a black box. In a sense, we're trying to find a way to work around and measure data that the LLMs are currently locking up. Plus, there are new AI visibility tools popping up left and right as GEO grows as a specialty. A few tools I tested that hit on a lot of the important features and almost made the list include: Goodie , Amplitude , AthenaHQ , Am I on AI? , Rankshift , XFunnel , Knowatoa , Waikay , Evertune , Superlines , RankScale , Scrunch , and SISTRIX . Yes, it's a little messy and definitely imperfect, but waiting for perfect data means missing the opportunity to shape how AI platforms talk about your brand right now—and that's a risk no forward-thinking marketer can afford to take. text: The 7 best AI brand visibility tracking tools for 2026, ranked by platform coverage and revenue attribution. Compare tools for monitoring brand mentions, sentiment, citation sources, and product recommendations across AI search. Your next customer might meet your brand in a paragraph you did not write. An assistant could recommend the wrong product, repeat outdated pricing, or describe a competitor more convincingly. Your website analytics alone will not tell you which of those happened. An AI brand visibility tracking tool records whether your brand appears in sampled answers, how it is described, and which sources are cited. It helps you inspect the recommendation before a shopper reaches your website. Coverage and collection methods differ by provider. This guide compares seven options by their intended use: Profound, Otterly, Peec AI, Nightwatch, SE Visible by SE Ranking, Ahrefs Brand Radar, and Alhena AI. The best AI search monitoring tool for your business depends on what you need to learn, not just how many engines appear on its homepage. Part one: Tracking or optimization? They are different purchases Tracking tells you where you stand. A monitoring tool can collect brand mentions, sentiment, answer position, and citation sources. Optimization is the work you do afterward: correcting product information, improving useful pages, and addressing gaps in external coverage. The distinction matters for budgeting. Buying a dashboard does not buy better recommendations. Someone still has to investigate the findings, decide what needs changing, and check the result. Traditional SEO and AI search monitoring should work together. Use keyword research to understand demand, then write the fuller questions a buyer might ask an assistant. Keep your SEO tool for the organic-search work it supports; add answer-level monitoring for the questions a conventional position report does not resolve. Do not abandon the basics. Established SEO practices remain relevant to Google AI Overviews and AI Mode; Google says there is no special optimization requirement for inclusion. [3] Start with a baseline you can maintain. Expand the program when the findings create decisions, rather than buying coverage nobody has time to use. For the next stage, read our guide to choosing and optimizing an AI visibility tool . Part two: How to evaluate the tools Use the same test questions for every vendor you trial. We recommend a starting set of 40 prompts across five categories: direct brand questions, category recommendations, comparisons, pricing, and factual accuracy. For example, an ecommerce team could test “Which fragrance-free moisturizers suit dry skin?” alongside questions about its own products. A software company would use different buying criteria. Neither should rely entirely on prompts containing its brand name. Check four things: which AI platforms the tool queries, whether its reported appearances match its saved responses, whether it exposes source URLs, and whether its summary calculations are explained. Keep the prompt, date, location, and collected answer together so another person can review the evidence. Best for: Teams that already use Ahrefs for research. Limitation: Confirm the included datasets, refresh settings, and custom-query capacity rather than assuming one allowance covers everything. Part three: How a brand visibility score is built Before you compare vendors, establish what each number means. For your own reporting, use this starting definition: Mention rate = collected responses naming your brand ÷ total eligible responses collected × 100. For an illustrative sample, 24 qualifying responses out of 100 produce a 24% rate. Count an answer once for this calculation even when it repeats the name. A different metric can count total appearances, but it needs a different label. Share of voice adds a competitive denominator. Decide whether you are comparing total appearances, responses containing each brand, or position-weighted recommendations. Document that choice before using the result in competitor benchmarking. A composite visibility score may also weight engines or answer positions. Do not compare two vendors' totals without comparing their inputs. Keep the same prompt set, market, and time window when evaluating movement. Your dashboard should offer a simple overview without hiding the evidence. Ask for the formula, sample counts, missing-response treatment, and exports. A score is most useful when the people reading it can explain why it changed. Part four: Mentions, sentiment, and citation sources Mention tracking: Did the brand appear? A mention establishes that a name appeared in a collected response. It does not, by itself, establish endorsement. Ask your vendor to distinguish a recommendation from a passing reference, comparison, or warning. For a product business, also distinguish the company name from the exact item. Alhena's product-level approach is designed around that distinction. Sentiment analysis: How was the brand described? Sentiment analysis evaluates the tone or framing of a response. Peec and Profound advertise this capability, while Nightwatch documents positive, neutral, and negative classifications. Use the label as a review cue. “Expensive but durable” might support your positioning; “cheap but unreliable” might not. Neither statement should be judged by counting positive words alone. Keep a separate accuracy check. Sentiment and factual correctness are different review questions, and a positive description should still be checked against product facts. Citation attribution: What supporting pages were shown? Citation reporting identifies the URLs an assistant visibly references. These could include your pages, a review, or a publisher's comparison. Products such as Otterly and Peec expose source information for investigation. Do not treat a visible citation list as a complete account of a model's reasoning or training data. For your workflow, record the source, read the claim, and decide whether the correction belongs on your site or elsewhere. The practical sequence is to track the appearance, inspect the description, and investigate the evidence. Part five: How accurate is any of this? Separate collection coverage from extraction accuracy . The first asks whether a sample represents the questions you care about. The second asks whether the tool correctly read the responses it actually collected. During a trial, select five useful prompts and run repeated checks with consistent location and session settings. Save the answers. Compare the tool's extracted results with those saved texts, not only with a fresh query that may produce different wording. Manually check brand aliases, product names, citations, and sentiment labels. Ask whether the vendor captures the consumer interface, an API response, or another dataset. Then ask how it handles failed requests and answers with no sources. For a proposed test, five prompts checked five times give you 25 responses to inspect. That is a debugging exercise, not proof that you have sampled the entire market. Do not report a small shift as a breakthrough without checking the underlying sample. Consistency makes monitoring useful; false precision makes it harder to trust. Part six: How to build an AI search monitoring workflow A useful AI search visibility program should end with a decision, not another report. Use this workflow to connect monitoring with SEO, product content, and commercial priorities. Start with buyer questions, not a longer keyword list Build your prompt library around actual decisions: product suitability, alternatives, price, materials, ingredients, delivery, and use cases. Separate branded questions from discovery questions so you can see whether people must already know you to find you. Choose the AI search engine coverage your audience needs. Treat Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode as separate surfaces. Ask explicitly about Claude, Copilot, and Grok rather than assuming they are included in a provider's “all engines” claim. Decide what the monitoring tool should track Ask a simple question: What should this tool track that will change our next action? Start with your brand, priority products, relevant rivals, and the pages cited in their recommendations. Use a fixed comparison set for each AI engine. When you add a competitor, note the date; otherwise a change in the denominator can look like a change in performance. Build a dashboard that shows the response, source, market, date, and next action. Track recommendation quality separately from simple presence. A marketing team should be able to tell whether the problem is missing coverage, incorrect information, or weak differentiation. Add competitor context without losing the question For each priority prompt, inspect what the recommended alternative does better in the answer. Does the response explain a feature, cite a comparison, or repeat a claim absent from your own pages? Scrunch is an additional option to evaluate when you also need site-crawl diagnostics. Alongside response monitoring, Scrunch advertises citation research and tools for investigating how automated systems access your content. It is outside this guide's seven main profiles. Add it to a shortlist when those diagnostics address a specific need, not simply to make the list longer. Turn findings into content fixes Assign one owner to each finding. Correct an outdated product detail at its authoritative source. Clarify a use case on the relevant product page. Where an independent publisher has the facts wrong, request a documented correction rather than demanding favorable coverage. For Alhena users, the product-level question is practical: which item should this buyer have discovered, and what information was missing? Use the answer to prioritize the next page review. Keep important information accessible as text and ensure structured data matches what a visitor sees. Google explicitly includes those checks in its guidance. Generative engine optimization should not become a reason to neglect sound SEO or write for machines instead of customers. [3] Connect the work to outcomes Track completed fixes against the original questions, then review the next comparable sample. Put observable referral visits and purchases beside the monitoring report in your analytics, not inside the same metric. As a reporting rule, do not claim a sale from an appearance you cannot connect to a visit or transaction. Use separate labels for observed referrals, assisted outcomes, and hypotheses. This gives the marketing team an insight it can defend, rather than a bigger number it cannot explain. Frequently asked questions What solutions provide a brand visibility score across multiple answer engines? Peec AI and Profound offer multi-engine reporting; Alhena provides product-level visibility across major engines. Their definitions and plan coverage differ. Ask for both an engine-level view and the calculation behind any combined score; a single total should not conceal where your brand is absent. What are the best AI search monitoring tools for a small team? Begin with the smallest paid setup that covers your essential questions. Otterly offers a $29 monthly entry plan with daily checks; Alhena offers a limited free snapshot for an initial look. Those are different services, so compare recurring coverage, not just the starting price. [13] What criteria matter when selecting AI brand monitoring software? Prioritize relevant engine coverage, collection methods, source URLs, exports, and a manageable review workflow. Test sentiment labels and brand-name matching using saved responses. Ask how often your selected plan refreshes and what happens when requests fail. A useful brand monitor should make its evidence inspectable, not merely display a percentage. How do I evaluate platforms for tracking visibility with AI agents? An AI agent can help organize prompts or summarize findings, but automation does not replace validation. Require a saved response, source URL, timestamp, and collection context wherever applicable. Test the same questions across trial accounts and inspect missing results. Judge the tracker by evidence you can reproduce, not the volume of summaries it produces. Which tools combine AI search visibility with sentiment analysis? Peec AI, Profound, Nightwatch, and SE Visible advertise sentiment-related reporting. During evaluation, read the underlying response alongside each label. Ask whether the system distinguishes tone about your brand from tone about the wider category and whether a human can correct misclassifications. What are the best tools for measuring ChatGPT brand visibility? Choose a tool that preserves responses and explains its sampling method. Profound's entry plan focuses on ChatGPT, while Nightwatch includes assistant-response tracking alongside organic-search work. Before purchasing, test the questions your customers ask and confirm the number of repeated checks included. How can I check whether an AI answer represents my brand accurately? Compare its factual claims with current product pages, policies, and documentation. Check pricing, availability, features, and intended use. Record errors separately from tone, because a complimentary answer can still be wrong. When an AI-generated response cites a page, inspect that page before deciding where the correction belongs. How do I measure brand mentions in AI search? Choose a fixed question set and collect comparable responses over a defined period. Record whether each answer names the brand, then divide qualifying responses by eligible responses collected. Track changes using the same settings. Keep raw mention counts separate from percentages and retain the sample size beside each result. Which platforms send alerts when visibility changes? Scrunch advertises alerts and scheduled reporting. For any vendor, confirm the specific triggers, delivery channels, thresholds, and plan requirements before buying. Scrunch's broader workflow also includes source and crawl investigation, but an alert is only useful when someone owns the response. How often should I check the data? Use a weekly review as a starting routine, with faster checks during an important launch or a known accuracy issue. Match the review to the collection schedule: opening a monthly-updated dashboard every day will not create new evidence. Reserve time to act on the findings, not just monitor them. Can an SEO platform replace a dedicated AI visibility tracker? Only when its answer-monitoring capabilities cover your actual requirements. Ahrefs Brand Radar and SE Ranking's AI Search add-on provide options alongside broader search workflows. Test the prompt controls, sources, and exports independently of the familiar SEO features. Traditional rank tracking alone does not answer whether an assistant recommended the right product. How does Alhena help ecommerce brands track AI search visibility? Alhena tracks product-level presence and analyzes how items appear in shopping responses, including details such as pricing, ratings, and positioning. It also offers product-page Q&A and citation-strategy capabilities. That helps a retailer investigate why the brand is recognized but a commercially important item is overlooked. [12] Will adding keywords make AI search engines cite my brand? No keyword count guarantees a citation. Use relevant terms where they clarify the answer, support claims with evidence, and keep product information consistent. Google says its AI features require no special optimization beyond established search practices. A clearer page can still go uncited; measure outcomes rather than assuming an editing score predicts them. [3] What the data will tell you and what to do about it Choose one recurring problem, fix it, and monitor the same question again. Perhaps a comparison misses your strongest use case. Perhaps an AI-generated description carries an old price. Perhaps an assistant recognizes the company but never recommends the item that fits the buyer. The useful insight is not merely that your visibility moved. It is that you can explain the change and choose the next action. Learn more about what your agency could build with us. Book a demo of Profound and turn AI search into a profitable service line. AI visibility tools for marketing agencies frequently asked questions (FAQs) What does an AI visibility tool do for an agency? It shows you how your clients are represented inside answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, then helps you do something about it. For an agency, the useful versions go past a single visibility score: they manage every client account from one place, let you audit a prospect before a pitch, generate or guide the content that closes gaps, and tie AI activity back to traffic and pipeline so you have something concrete to show on a client call. Which of these tools have real agency programs? A handful are built with agencies in mind rather than bolting on a discount. Profound's Agency Mode runs client workspaces and pitch environments; Scrunch offers referral commission, prospecting licenses, and co-marketing funds; Otterly runs a partner program with workspace management and a directory; AthenaHQ refers qualified leads by focus area; Rankability was designed for agencies from the start; and AIclicks has a partner directory with revenue share. The rest are usable by agencies but weren't built around the agency motion. Can these tools help win new clients, not just serve existing ones? Yes, and it's one of the clearest dividing lines. Pitch environments (Profound and AthenaHQ) let you pull up a prospect's real AI visibility on a sales call instead of describing the problem in the abstract, and Profound converts that pitch workspace straight into a live account when the deal closes. Lead-referral programs (AthenaHQ) and partner directories (Otterly, AIclicks) add an inbound channel on top. How do agencies prove AEO ROI to clients? Because AI answers often don't produce a click, attribution takes more than a traffic report. The strongest signal is crawler-level analytics tied to outcomes: Profound's Agent Analytics traces the chain from AI crawler visit to citation to human traffic to conversion through a GA4 connection. Most agencies pair that with self-reported attribution on demo forms and mentions in sales calls, building a picture across several directional signals rather than chasing one perfect number. Does an agency need a dedicated AEO tool, or is an SEO platform enough? SEO suites like Semrush, Ahrefs, BrightEdge, and Conductor have all added AI visibility, and for agencies already living in those tools, the convenience is real. But each one treats AI as an add-on, with narrower engine coverage, keyword-derived rather than real prompt data, and no AEO-specific content workflows. Plenty of agencies run both: an SEO platform for keywords, backlinks, and rank tracking, and a purpose-built AEO platform for the AI side. How many answer engines should an agency track? Enough to cover where your clients' buyers actually are. ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews are the baseline every serious tool should hit. From there, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, Meta AI, and DeepSeek matter to different degrees depending on a client's audience and region. Tools that cap at four or five engines leave blind spots in your reporting; the ones tracking all 10 give you the full picture across a varied client base.

title: 6 AI Visibility Tools to Track Your Brand Across LLMs (2026)
headings: What to Look For in an LLM Tracking Tool
Whichever Tool You Choose, Just Start Tracking
text: LLMs like ChatGPT and Gemini are quickly becoming the first place people turn when researching brands, products, and services. The challenge is that most companies still have no real visibility into how they appear inside these answers. That blind spot is growing. AI responses shape perception long before someone reaches your site. And the early data is clear. Backlinko still brings in hundreds of thousands of visitors from organic search… But LLM-driven traffic is up 800% year-over-year. And accelerating. This is why AI visibility matters. It is no longer about traffic alone. It is about presence, accuracy, and how your brand is positioned inside the systems people trust for answers. To stay ahead, you need the right tools. I’ve tested more than a dozen LLM tracking platforms across enterprise solutions and newer entrants. Not all of them are fully mature, and I don’t know which ones will survive in the long run, but each one highlights a different direction the market is moving. Here are six tools worth considering. What to Look For in an LLM Tracking Tool There are some free AI visibility checkers out there, which are great for getting an introductory look at how your brand is faring in LLM answers. But if you need more data and context, you’ll likely need to go the paid route. A lot of paid LLM tracking tools look impressive at first glance. Once you dig in, many fall short. The most common issues are fragile scraping setups, limited coverage, or dashboards that look polished but fail to surface the insights that actually matter. Here’s what to consider: Real scale: Because AI responses vary significantly run-to-run, you need a large enough prompt sample to get a statistically meaningful read on your visibility. Thousands of prompts, run from the UI, not just the APIs. Otherwise, you miss key results (like tables and maps). Multi-engine coverage: ChatGPT is table stakes. Top tools also track Google AI Mode, AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude, and Copilot — and break out visibility by platform. That matters: an analysis of 3.7 million AI citations found that 91% of cited URLs appear in just one LLM , so strong performance on one platform tells you almost nothing about the others. Visibility percentage, not position data: SparkToro research running nearly 3,000 prompts across multiple AI platforms found that these produce identical brand recommendations less than 1 in 100 times, and identical ordering less than 1 in 1,000 times . So, “AI rankings” are statistically meaningless. The key metric you need is aggregate visibility percentage: how often your brand appears across a representative sample of prompts. Actionable insights: Breakdowns by model, topic, sentiment. Bonus if it flags missed opportunities and quick wins. Roadmap momentum: Is the team shipping fast? If not, skip it. Global support: Need multi-language prompts or market-level insights? Not all tools can do it. Enterprise-ready: Solid support. Clean data policies. And a team that’s leading the space, not chasing it. 1. Semrush Semrush brings SEO and generative engine optimization (GEO) tools together in one platform. And I think it’s the right approach: if you want to understand why ChatGPT or Google AI Mode describes your brand the way it does, you can’t isolate LLM results from the web signals those models rely on. That’s why Semrush now offers three ways to work with AI search data — each with a different level of depth: AI Visibility Toolkit Who it’s for: anyone actively doing SEO or content marketing — which, realistically, is every brand with a website. text: Summarize this blog post with: ChatGPT Perplexity Claude Grok In this article, you’ll learn which AI visibility optimization tools are worth your budget, which ones oversell and underdeliver, and how to evaluate them based on the features that actually move the needle for small and mid-market teams. You’ll also see how traditional SEO tools like Ahrefs and Semrush stack up against purpose-built platforms, and why the best tool for tracking AI visibility should also help you improve it. We spent 90+ days testing every tool on this list across real brand projects. We tracked the same prompts, compared outputs, and documented what each platform can and cannot do. This is the honest breakdown. Table of Contents Why You Need an AI Visibility Tool (and Why Your SEO Stack Isn’t Enough) More buyers are getting answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude before they ever visit Google. These AI engines don’t just list links. They describe your product, compare you to competitors, and shape purchase decisions in a single response. Your existing SEO tools were not built for this. They track keywords, backlinks, and SERP positions. They do not tell you what ChatGPT says when someone asks “best CRM for startups” or whether Perplexity recommends your competitor instead of you. That gap is where AI visibility optimization tools come in. They monitor how AI engines talk about your brand, track your position in AI-generated answers, and give you the data to improve what’s being said. But not all tools are equal. Some only monitor. Some only track one or two engines. Some charge enterprise prices for features you can get at a fraction of the cost. Here’s how to sort them out. What to Look for in an AI Visibility Tool Before picking a tool, you need to know which capabilities actually matter. Based on our testing, here are the six that separate useful platforms from expensive dashboards. Prompt-level tracking. You need to monitor specific prompts daily, not just see a one-time snapshot. AI responses shift constantly, and weekly or monthly checks miss the changes that matter. Multi-engine coverage. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews each have different source preferences. A tool that only covers one or two engines gives you a partial picture. Citation analytics. Knowing you’re mentioned is not enough. You need to see which URLs AI engines cite when they mention your brand and your competitors. That tells you where to focus your content efforts. AI traffic attribution. The best tools connect AI mentions to actual traffic. If you can’t tie visibility to GA4 sessions, you’re guessing about ROI. Content creation and optimization. Monitoring without action is just a dashboard. Look for tools that help you write content designed to earn AI citations and optimize existing pages that are being ignored. Competitive benchmarking. You need to see who’s winning the prompts you care about, what sources they’re cited from, and where your gaps are. The table below shows how each tool stacks up against these criteria. Connect GA4, and AI Traffic Analytics shows you exactly which AI engines send visitors to your site, which pages they land on, and how that traffic trends month over month. The AI Content Optimizer audits existing URLs and rewrites them with specific citation-earning improvements. The Agent Builder is the real differentiator. This is not a simple automation layer. It is a programmable substrate with 180+ production-ready nodes , 34 pre-built data recipes, and direct integrations with GA4, Google Search Console, DataForSEO, Semrush, HubSpot, Notion, WordPress, Slack, and every major LLM. You can build agents that run on a schedule, fire on a webhook, or execute on demand. Here are real examples of what teams build with it: A Monday board prep agent that pulls your AI visibility data, GA4 traffic, competitor shifts, and new HubSpot deals into an executive summary delivered to Slack every Monday at 7am. That replaces a 4-hour analyst workflow. A brief-to-publish pipeline triggered when a content brief moves to “approved” in Notion. It generates research, builds an outline, writes a full draft with brand voice injected, scores it for AI citation readiness, and publishes to WordPress if the score passes. If it fails, it sends the gaps to the writer via Slack. A crisis early-warning agent that scans brand mentions every 15 minutes, filters for negative sentiment above a threshold, and alerts your PR team with the source URLs and a drafted response before your CEO hears about it. With 180+ nodes across 16 categories, the practical surface is millions of useful configurations. A CMO ships board-grade intelligence on cadence without an analyst. An agency turns reporting day into a background process. A content team runs a publish pipeline that gates on quality automatically. These are not templates. You compose from primitives. Best for: Teams that want to monitor, create, optimize, and automate AI visibility from a single platform without paying enterprise prices. 2. Profound Profound is the most funded platform in this category, with $155M raised and a $1B valuation. It tracks brand visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews. Its standout feature is Prompt Volumes, panel data from opted-in consumers showing what real users ask AI engines, with regional and demographic breakdowns. No one else ships this dataset. The platform also offers Conversation Explorer for finding buyer queries, Agent Analytics for tracking AI bot crawling activity on your site, and a content workflow called Profound Agents for generating and publishing AEO content. The tradeoffs are significant. Profound does not support multi-account management, so agencies managing five clients need five separate accounts. The Agents feature is scoped to AEO content workflows only, not general marketing ops. And pricing starts at $99/month for a ChatGPT-only plan with 50 prompts. Multi-platform coverage starts at $399/month, and the features most people associate with Profound (Prompt Volumes, full API access, unlimited seats) are enterprise-only at custom pricing. Best for: Enterprise teams with dedicated analysts who need panel-level prompt volume data and can justify $399+/month. 3. AthenaHQ AthenaHQ covers 8 AI engines on every plan and offers a feature called Action Center that turns visibility gaps into structured, assignable optimization tasks. Founded by former Google Search and DeepMind engineers, it has strong technical foundations. The challenge is pricing and predictability. AthenaHQ uses a credit-based model starting at $295/month for 3,600 credits. Every AI response you track consumes credits. Heavy monitoring across 8 engines burns through credits fast, and overage costs $100 per 1,250 additional credits. The most advanced features, including the ACE Citation Engine, persona targeting, and API access, are locked behind an enterprise tier at $2,000+/month. The credit model makes monthly spend hard to predict. If you’re tracking 50 prompts across 8 engines daily, you can exceed your credit limit before mid-month. Teams that prefer fixed subscription pricing will find this frustrating. Best for: Single-market teams comfortable with credit-based pricing who need structured optimization workflows and broad engine coverage. 4. Peec AI Peec AI is the most accessible platform on this list. It offers clean, straightforward GEO tracking with daily prompt monitoring, sentiment scoring, ranking analysis, and share-of-voice charts across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Grok, and DeepSeek. The interface is intuitive and the learning curve is minimal. Peec is good for teams that want foundational visibility data without complexity. But it leans heavily toward passive monitoring. There’s no AI traffic attribution, no content creation or optimization workflows, and no way to take direct action from the data inside the platform. You’ll need to export insights and act on them in other tools. Pricing: ~$95 to $199/month. Best for: Small agencies and marketing teams who want a quick, affordable view of AI visibility without needing content or automation features. 5. Ahrefs (Brand Radar AI) Ahrefs extended its brand monitoring suite with Brand Radar AI, which tracks how your brand appears in AI-generated answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews. It merges traditional web-based brand monitoring (unlinked mentions, linked mentions, ownership of AI Overviews) with emerging AI visibility signals. Brand Radar is designed to live inside the existing Ahrefs ecosystem. It’s a signal layer, not a full GEO workflow. There’s no prompt-level search, no daily prompt tracking, no AI traffic attribution, and no content optimization for AI visibility. If you already pay for Ahrefs and want a basic sense of how AI engines reference your brand, Brand Radar adds value. If you need to actively improve your AI visibility, you’ll outgrow it quickly. Pricing: Starts at $199/month (requires an Ahrefs subscription). Best for: Teams already using Ahrefs who want brand monitoring extended to AI contexts. 6. Semrush (via Otterly) Semrush offers AI visibility through Otterly, a dedicated add-on that tracks how your brand appears in AI-generated content. It monitors visibility and sentiment across ChatGPT, Perplexity, SearchGPT, and Gemini, with weekly updated reports and competitive benchmarking. The weekly update cadence is the biggest limitation. AI responses change daily, and weekly snapshots miss shifts that matter. Otterly also lacks prompt-level detail pages, on-demand prompt search, and AI traffic attribution. It works as a bridge between keyword visibility and AI prompt visibility for teams already invested in Semrush, but it is not a standalone solution. Pricing: $99/month per domain (on top of your Semrush subscription). Best for: Semrush users who want to add basic AI visibility reporting to their existing workflow. 7. Surfer (AI Tracker) Surfer’s AI Tracker lets you monitor how specific prompts are answered by ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity. You choose from 25, 100, or 300 prompts depending on your plan, and Surfer refreshes a portion of them daily. The tracking sits alongside Surfer’s content optimization tools, which makes it appealing for writers and SEO teams. But the AI tracking itself is lightweight. There’s no prompt suggestion engine, limited citation analysis, no competitive benchmarking dashboard, and no AI traffic integration. Pricing: Starts at $95/month for 25 prompts, scaling to $495/month for 300 prompts, on top of a base Surfer subscription. Best for: Content teams already using Surfer who want to add basic AI prompt monitoring. 8. Wix (AI Visibility Overview) Wix offers a native AI Visibility Overview inside its platform. It auto-generates industry-relevant prompts, tests your visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity, and returns a proprietary AI Visibility Score. It also includes competitor benchmarking, sentiment analysis, GA4-based traffic tracking, and generates an LLMs.txt file for controlling bot access. For Wix users, this is surprisingly capable as a built-in feature. But it’s limited to Wix-hosted sites, the prompts are auto-generated rather than custom, and there’s no content optimization workflow or competitive depth beyond basic benchmarking. Best for: Small businesses on Wix who want AI visibility insights without adopting a separate tool. How to Use AI Visibility Data Alongside Your SEO Workflow Here’s something most AI visibility articles won’t tell you: SEO is not dead . AI search is an additional organic channel, not a replacement for traditional search. The brands winning in AI answers are the same ones investing in quality content, technical SEO, and topical authority. The difference is that now your content has to work for AI models too. That means the smartest approach is to layer AI visibility on top of your existing SEO workflow, not replace it. Use AI traffic data to validate what’s working. Once you connect GA4 to a tool like Analyze AI , look at which pages receive AI referral traffic. These pages are already doing something right for AI engines. Study the patterns. What topics they cover, how they’re structured, what sources they cite. Then double down on what works. Discover prompts you should target with content. Prompt discovery surfaces the queries where your competitors appear and you don’t. These are content gaps you can fill. Many of these prompts map directly to traditional search keywords too, which means one piece of content can win in both channels. Monitor your brand narrative across engines. AI engines don’t just rank you. They describe you. AI Sentiment Monitoring and the Perception Map show you exactly how each engine frames your brand. If ChatGPT describes your product as “affordable but limited” while Perplexity calls it “full-featured,” you have a messaging problem to fix with targeted content. Automate the repetitive work. If you’re manually checking AI answers, pulling competitor data, writing reports, or scanning for negative mentions, you’re spending hours on work that should run in the background. An Agent Builder with scheduled triggers, webhook integrations, and direct CRM connections turns these tasks into set-and-forget processes. You focus on strategy. The agents handle operations. Which AI Visibility Tool Is Right for You? If you’re just exploring the space and want a low-commitment starting point, Peec AI ($95/month) or Wix (included) give you basic visibility data without complexity. If you’re already invested in a traditional SEO suite and want to add AI visibility as a signal, Ahrefs Brand Radar , Semrush Otterly , or Surfer AI Tracker extend what you already use, but none of them offer the depth to actively compete in AI search. If you need enterprise-grade panel data and your budget supports it, Profound ($399+/month) delivers unique prompt volume insights that no one else has. If you want the most complete platform at a price point that makes sense for small and mid-market teams, Analyze AI ($99/month) gives you daily tracking, multi-engine coverage, citation analytics, GA4 traffic attribution, a full content creation and optimization stack, and a 180+ node Agent Builder that extends into SEO research, CRM, CMS, email, and virtually anything else your marketing operations need. The question is not whether you need an AI visibility tool. You do. The question is whether you want one that monitors, or one that monitors, creates, optimizes, and automates. AI assistants recommend the same handful of tools again and again. We track 12 prompts about AI SEO, GEO and AEO tools in Surfer (for example "What are the best AI SEO tools?", "Best GEO tools" and "best AEO tools") across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode. Over 30 days (24 September to 23 October 2026), the answers cited 738 different URLs 10,779 times, and these brands were named most often: Most-mentioned tools when people ask AI about AI SEO, GEO and AEO tools Share of AI answers that mention each tool, across 12 prompts in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Overviews and AI Mode, 24 Sep – 23 Oct 2026. Hover or tap a bar for its average position. Mention rate Average position Source: Surfer, 12 tracked prompts, 24 Sep – 23 Oct 2026. Positive Surfer Show data Three patterns stand out: A few brands own the category. Semrush appears in 90% of answers; Ahrefs and Surfer each in 66%. Specialist AI visibility tools appear less often: Profound in 48% of answers, Peec AI in 28%. AI leans on video, vendor pages and roundups. The most cited domains were youtube.com (610 citations), semrush.com (515), onelittleweb.com (364), ahrefs.com (337) and reddit.com (302), followed by independent roundups on zapier.com and technologyadvice.com. Answers vary by engine and by run. Twelve prompts are a sample, not a census. Track your own prompts over weeks before drawing conclusions. Prompts that ask specifically for AI visibility trackers, such as "What are the best AI visibility tools?" and "Best alternatives to Profound", surface a slightly different set. In the first runs of a second Surfer project with 26 such prompts (to 24 October 2026), the tools named most were Semrush, Profound, Otterly.AI, Ahrefs and Peec AI, followed by SE Ranking, Scrunch, AthenaHQ, ZipTie and Rankscale. Every one of them is reviewed below. What do AI visibility tools track? AI visibility tools track whether AI answers mention and cite your brand, and how that compares with competitors. Most report the same core metrics, under slightly different names: AI visibility score: a 0–100 index of how visible your brand is across tracked prompts and AI engines (see how a visibility score works ). Mention rate: the share of AI answers that name your brand. Average position: where your brand appears in the answer, with 1 meaning first. Share of voice: your mentions compared with competitors' for the same prompts. Citations and sources: which of your pages AI links to, and which third-party sites it cites when it mentions you or your competitors. Your own most-cited pages show what's already working. Sentiment: whether AI describes your brand positively, neutrally or negatively. Prompt tracking: the questions you monitor, often grouped into topics, with results per prompt and per engine. Query fan-outs: the searches an AI engine runs behind the scenes to answer a prompt (Surfer and Otterly.AI show these). AI traffic and crawlers: visits from AI assistants and how AI bots crawl your site (for example Profound, Writesonic, Promptwatch and Similarweb). Mentions without citations tell you AI knows your brand; citations tell you which pages earn it. Track both. What features should an AI visibility tracker have? A good AI visibility tracker covers the AI platforms your buyers use, reads real answers, shows citations as well as mentions, benchmarks competitors over time and points to what to fix. Use this checklist when you compare trackers: Feature What to look for Tools that do it well Coverage of major AI platforms ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode at minimum; Claude and Copilot if your buyers use them AthenaHQ, Rankscale, Promptwatch, Profound (Enterprise) Real-interface data Answers collected from the apps people use, not only from APIs Surfer, Profound, Peec AI, SE Visible, Writesonic, Promptwatch Citation tracking The URLs and domains each answer cites, and whether they mention you Surfer, Peec AI, ZipTie, Ahrefs Brand Radar Visibility score and visibility trends A trend over weeks, not a one-off snapshot Surfer, Semrush, SE Ranking Competitor benchmarking Share of voice against the brands you choose, per prompt and engine Surfer, Peec AI, Scrunch, Semrush Recommendations Prompts you lose, sources to pitch, pages to update Surfer (Mention Gap and Content Editor), Peec AI, Otterly.AI, SE Ranking SEO and AI side by side Rankings and AI citations in one place, to compare AI and traditional search performance SE Ranking, Semrush, Ahrefs, Nightwatch, ZipTie AI traffic and crawlers AI referral visits and bot activity on your site Profound, Writesonic, Promptwatch, Similarweb Prompt research Which questions people ask AI in your category Semrush, Profound, Similarweb A single score is the least useful part. Prompt-level detail, the sources behind each answer and a clear next step matter more, because they tell your content and digital PR teams what to do on Monday. How did we choose the best AI visibility tools? We ran the tools we tested with the same sites, similar prompts and comparable competitors, to see how consistent the visibility data was and how useful the insights were in practice. We also compared notes with SEO teams and content marketers who use these tools daily, and checked which tools AI answers and the top Google results recommend. Three criteria mattered most: Prompt control: can you see and edit the exact prompts being tracked? Explanations: does the tool show why a brand appears in AI responses, or doesn't, through the sources and citations behind each answer? Next steps: does the AI visibility data lead to concrete actions that improve your brand visibility? We also weighed which AI engines each tool covers, how it collects answers, and the price per tracked prompt. Collection method matters: in Surfer's study of API results vs. scraped AI answers , roughly 75% of the brands named didn't overlap between the two methods. Tools that read the real interfaces people use (Surfer, Profound, Peec AI, SE Visible, Writesonic and Promptwatch say they do) are closer to what your buyers actually see. 1. Surfer Best for: teams that want to track AI visibility and improve it in the same tool. Surfer measures how often you show up in AI answers, which websites AI search engines cite, and, more importantly, helps you create content that's more likely to be mentioned by large language models. Its AI visibility tracking sits next to the Content Editor, so the data and the fix live in one place. To get started, enter your site's domain and list your focus topics. Surfer generates prompts your ideal customers are likely to ask AI assistants, and you can add any prompts you want to track yourself. Surfer reads the answers in the same interfaces people use, not through an API, because API results and real AI answers often name different brands. The Overview page shows your brand's AI visibility score, mention rate across AI models and average position in AI responses. You can benchmark competitor visibility on the same metrics and filter to the competitors you care about. For each prompt, you can open the full detail: which brands were mentioned, which sources were cited and which fan-out queries the AI ran. The Mention Gap report lists sources that name your competitors but not you, which makes a ready-made outreach list. We use the fan-out queries to research outlines, so our content is optimized for both AI search and Google's blue links. That covers AI search visibility tracking, and it's where most AI visibility tools stop. Surfer goes further with content optimization: the Content Editor shows the facts AI answers include for your topic, so you can cover them and give AI engines a reason to cite you. Surfer's research found that pages cited in AI Overviews covered 31% of a topic's key facts , versus 24% for pages that weren't cited. Pricing: the AI Search Analytics plan costs $82/month billed yearly ($95 month to month) and tracks 50 prompts daily across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, with Mention Gap, brand sentiment, five brand spaces and MCP. The Standard plan ($99/month yearly) adds the Content Editor and tracks 25 prompts weekly in ChatGPT; Pro ($182/month yearly) tracks 50 prompts daily in all five engines with the content tools. You can start for free. Pros: Reads real AI answers, not just API results Connects AI visibility tracking with SEO and content optimization in one platform Mention gap, sentiment and source reports point to outreach targets Cons: Doesn't track Claude or Microsoft Copilot The Content Editor isn't in the AI Search Analytics plan; you need Standard or higher 2. Profound Best for: enterprise brands that need depth, many engines and compliance. Profound is an enterprise AI visibility platform. Its Answer Engine Insights show how AI engines describe your brand, with citation analytics, sentiment and a FactCheck agent for inaccurate claims. Prompt Volumes estimate which questions people ask AI assistants in your category, Agent Analytics shows how AI crawlers access your site, and its AI Marketer agents turn the data into content and tasks. Profound says it captures answers from each engine's front-end interface rather than through API calls. Enterprise covers up to 9 engines, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, Claude and Google AI Overviews, and adds API access, CSV and JSON exports, SSO/SAML and SOC 2 compliance. Pricing: no public price for brands. A 7-day free trial tracks 50 prompts daily in ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews (prompts can't be customized on the trial); Enterprise pricing is custom. Agencies get separate plans. Pros: Among the broadest engine coverage here, including Copilot and Claude Enterprise features: SSO, SOC 2, API, exports Cons: No public pricing, so it's hard to budget for More than most small teams need See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Profound . 3. Peec AI Best for: marketing teams that want flexible prompt tracking with unlimited seats. Peec AI tracks your visibility, position, sentiment and share of voice against competitors, with source analytics that show which domains and URLs AI cites. Gap analysis and recommended actions point to where competitors appear and you don't, and crawl insights (via CDN integrations) show how AI bots access your site. On the Starter, Pro and Advanced plans you choose 3 models from ChatGPT, AI Mode, AI Overviews, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and Naver AI; Perplexity and Claude are paid add-ons. Peec says it collects answers through each platform's web interface. MCP is on every plan, the API starts on Pro and the Looker Studio connector on Advanced. Pricing: Starter costs €85/month (€70/month billed yearly) for 50 prompts, with unlimited users. Pro is €205/month (€180 yearly) for 150 prompts; Advanced is €425/month (€360 yearly) for 350 prompts with multi-country tracking. There's a free trial. Pros: Unlimited users on every plan Clear source and citation analytics Cons: Only 3 engines on the entry plan; Perplexity costs extra Priced in euros, so US costs move with the exchange rate See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Peec AI . 4. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit Best for: teams already using Semrush for SEO. Semrush's AI Visibility Toolkit approaches AI search from a familiar angle. You add a domain and competitors, and Semrush aggregates how those brands appear across AI generated answers. The dashboard centers on an AI visibility score out of 100, plus mentions, cited pages and monthly audience. You can drill down by region or AI platform to see which topics and prompts surface your brand. Prompt Research clusters AI questions around a topic with demand and difficulty signals, which helps you decide which prompts to track. The Brand Performance tab is a highlight: plain-language insights on what you're doing well and what to improve, plus share of voice, sentiment analysis and "narrative drivers," the domains and questions shaping how AI describes your brand. Pricing: the toolkit costs $99/month per domain for 25 prompts tracked daily, and 50 more prompts cost $60/month. It doesn't have its own free trial. Semrush One bundles start at $199/month with 50 prompts. Semrush's pricing page lists mentions from ChatGPT, Google AI, Gemini and Perplexity. Pros: Strong brand and competitor-level analysis Prompt research helps you find the questions worth tracking Cons: 25 prompts on the base plan is the fewest per dollar here Analysis-focused; content optimization happens in other Semrush tools See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Semrush . 5. Ahrefs Brand Radar Best for: large-scale brand visibility data without defining prompts first. Brand Radar is Ahrefs' AI visibility tool. Setup is simple: enter your brand domain, list competitors and choose your market. Instead of a fixed set of prompts you define, Brand Radar draws on Ahrefs' database of about 500 million prompts, so you get an AI visibility score almost immediately rather than waiting for fresh runs. The index covers ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode; Claude is available through custom prompts. You'll see AI share of voice, mentions, citations and estimated impressions, plus YouTube, TikTok and Reddit sources. Filters let you answer questions like where your brand is mentioned but not cited, or which third-party sites shape how AI describes your product. Pricing: Brand Radar AI starts at $199/month and is sold on its own, with a free Ahrefs account. Custom-prompt packages start at $50/month. Regular Ahrefs plans (from $129/month) include a small number of AI prompt checks, and Ahrefs also offers a free AI Visibility Checker. Pros: Instant data from a very large prompt database Powerful filters for analyzing thousands of results Cons: $199/month entry price Custom prompts, and Claude, cost extra See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Ahrefs . 6. Otterly.AI Best for: a simple, low-cost start with AI visibility monitoring. Otterly.AI tracks brand visibility, sentiment and cited sources across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot, with Google AI Mode, Gemini and Claude as add-ons. It includes weekly recommendations, query fan-out and prompt research tools, and GEO audits, and supports unlimited countries and languages. The Standard and Premium plans add an API, an MCP server, agent analytics and a Looker Studio connector. Semrush also offers an Otterly app in its App Center. Pricing: Lite costs $29/month ($25/month billed yearly) for 15 prompts; AI Mode and Gemini are $9/month each on Lite and Claude $29/month. Standard is $189/month for 100 prompts and Premium $489/month for 400. The 7-day free trial needs no card. Pros: Low entry price for a self-serve tracker Copilot included on the base plan Cons: Only 15 prompts on the entry plan Collection method isn't stated See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Otterly.AI . 7. SE Ranking's AI search tracking sits inside the same SEO platform where you manage keyword research, rank tracking and site audits. That's useful: when AI mentions shift, you can check whether rankings or page structure changed too. We added a domain and prompts, and the tracker collected brand mentions, link citations and position data, with competitor visibility side by side. The Insights feature turns AI visibility data into a to-do list: prompts where competitors are mentioned and you aren't, and frequently cited sources that don't mention you. AI Competitor Research analyzes any domain's AI presence without a project, and GA4 integration ties AI visibility to real traffic. SE Visible is SE Ranking's standalone AI visibility product. It tracks ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Mode and AI Overviews through the browser interface, not API results; SE Ranking says Claude is coming soon. Perplexity isn't covered yet. Pricing: SE Visible Basic costs $99/month ($79 yearly) for 200 prompts, with a 10-day free trial; Core is $189/month for 450 prompts. In SE Ranking, the AI Search add-on costs €79/month (€63.20 yearly) for 200 prompts in AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT. Pros: 200 prompts on the entry plan, the most of any tool here at that price Connects AI visibility with rank tracking, GA4 and the full SEO suite Cons: No Perplexity yet In-depth sentiment is still marked "coming soon" See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs SE Ranking . 8. Scrunch Best for: brands that want persona-level benchmarking and an AI agent experience layer. Scrunch tracks citations and benchmarks your visibility by competitor, persona, topic and region, and runs site audits for AI readiness. On Enterprise it adds the Agent Experience Platform (AXP), which serves AI-readable versions of your pages, plus API access and SSO. Scrunch says it collects answers through a combination of browser automation and official platform APIs, chosen per platform. Prompts run daily for the first 14 days, then every 72 hours by default. Pricing: Core costs $250/month for 125 prompts and 5,000 responses a month across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Copilot, with a 7-day trial. Enterprise is custom and covers 9 engines, adding Claude, Gemini, Meta AI, AI Mode and Grok. Agency Core costs $500/month. Pros: Persona and region benchmarking AI-readable page versions on Enterprise Cons: No Gemini or AI Mode on Core Mix of browser and API data See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Scrunch . 9. AthenaHQ Best for: teams that want many AI engines and a free starting point. AthenaHQ tracks sources and competitor insights and adds content recommendations with a content optimization agent. The free Essential plan covers ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini and Copilot; Starter adds AI Mode, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI and Mistral, for 11 engines in total. Pricing: AthenaHQ uses credits (1 credit = 1 AI response) instead of prompts. Essential is free with 300 credits; Starter costs $295/month ($245 billed yearly) with 3,600 credits and unlimited topics and prompts. API access and extra credits are paid add-ons. Pros: Free plan with five engines 11 engines on Starter Cons: Credit-based pricing is harder to compare Big jump from free to $295/month See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs AthenaHQ . 10. ZipTie Best for: analysts who want deep data and to pay only for the prompts and engines they track. ZipTie tracks brand mentions, citations and sentiment across seven AI engines: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and Bing's AI answers. It classifies cited sources by type, scores each brand with an "AI Success Score" and captures the Google and Bing top 10 next to each AI Overview check, so you can compare AI and organic results for the same query. Unlimited seats, projects, competitors and white-label reports come with every plan, and API and MCP access is a $10/month add-on. ZipTie's methodology page is upfront about the limits: it doesn't track AI crawlers or referral traffic and has no prompt-volume data. Pricing: instead of fixed tiers, you build a plan from prompts, refresh frequency and engines. The Starter preset tracks 30 prompts daily in ChatGPT, AI Overviews and Perplexity from $25.65/month, and annual billing takes 20% off. The 7-day trial (25 daily prompts) needs no card. Pros: Pay only for the prompts and engines you need AI answers and organic top 10 side by side Cons: The plan calculator takes some time to figure out No AI crawler or referral tracking 11. Writesonic Best for: teams that want AI visibility tracking, content creation and site fixes in one subscription. Writesonic has grown from an AI writer into an AI search visibility platform. Its AI Visibility Tracker is on every plan and, according to Writesonic, crawls AI platforms like a real user rather than through APIs. Every plan also includes AI Bot Analytics and monitoring of ads in ChatGPT and Google AI, and the Action Center (from Growth) suggests on-page and off-page fixes. Pricing: Starter costs $99/month ($79 yearly) for 50 prompts tracked daily in ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. Basic ($249/month) and Growth ($499/month) raise the limits; sentiment starts on Growth. Enterprise is custom and covers all nine platforms, including Perplexity, Claude, Copilot, Grok and AI Mode. You can start free. Pros: Tracking, content tools and AI bot analytics in one place Real-user collection, not APIs Cons: Self-serve plans cover only three engines Sentiment only from $499/month See the full side-by-side: Surfer vs Writesonic . 12. Rankscale Best for: spotting weaknesses before you start tracking, on a small budget. Rankscale starts with a website analysis that gives an AI search readiness score, split into content quality and relevance, authority and trust, technical SEO and page structure, and engagement. To track visibility, you set up a brand with its topics and competitors, then add search terms to monitor. It covers 17+ AI engines on every plan, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, DeepSeek, Mistral and Grok, with citation and sentiment analysis, query fan-outs and an MCP server. Rankscale reads some engines through their interfaces and others through APIs. Pricing: Essentials costs $17/month, billed yearly only, with 120 credits. Pro costs $99/month ($84 yearly) with 1,200 credits and adds Looker Studio, and there's a 7-day Pro trial with limited credits. Unused credits roll over from Pro up. Pros: Readiness audit shows what to fix before you track Low entry price with very broad engine coverage Cons: Credit-based limits take some getting used to Mixes interface and API data, depending on engine 13. LLM Pulse Best for: low-cost weekly tracking with paid add-on engines. LLM Pulse tracks share of voice, mentions and citations with recommendations, across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode, AI Overviews and Gemini on every plan. Claude, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI and others are paid add-ons. MCP is on all plans; sentiment starts on Growth, and the API and Looker Studio connector on Scale. Pricing: Starter costs €49/month (€40.83 yearly) for 50 prompts tracked weekly, or €79/month for daily tracking. Weekly plans include a 14-day trial; a payment method is required. Pros: 50 prompts for under €50 Many optional engines Cons: Daily tracking costs more No sentiment on Starter 14. Amplitude AI Visibility Best for: a free first look at your AI visibility. Amplitude's AI Visibility tool runs on its free plan. You enter your brand or website and get a report without defining prompts first; sign up to control prompts, region and language. The Prompts, Sources and Competitors tabs show visibility, average rank and citations by topic and prompt, and how you compare with each competitor. Pricing: included in every Amplitude plan, including Free, "with limited volumes." It tracks ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. Pros: Free, with a report before you set up prompts Solid competitor and source analysis Cons: Only two engines No content optimization beyond tracking What other AI visibility tools are worth knowing? Seven more AI monitoring tools come up often in AI answers and roundups. They didn't make our main list because they're enterprise-only, add-ons to another product, or newer, but each fits a specific need: Tool Best for Starting price AI engines Promptwatch Many engines plus crawler logs and content writing $95/mo (Essential, 50 prompts); 7-day trial ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, AI Mode, AI Overviews, DeepSeek and more on every plan Nightwatch Rank tracking with AI visibility on top €99/mo (€79 yearly) for 500 keywords and 50 prompts; 14-day trial ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Mode, AI Overviews Similarweb AI Search Intelligence AI visibility next to AI referral traffic $129/mo ($99 yearly) for 150 prompts ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Mode Keyword.com Credit-based AI checks next to rank tracking $9.80/mo ($7.83 yearly) for 20 credits; 14-day trial AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot; Claude, Perplexity and others via API HubSpot AI Search Grader and AEO A free one-off brand check; paid tracking for HubSpot teams Grader free; AEO $50/mo ($45 yearly) for 25 prompts ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity seoClarity (Clarity ArcAI) Enterprise SEO teams Custom; packages start at 500 prompts ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Mode, AI Overviews; Claude, Copilot, DeepSeek, Grok Conductor Enterprise AEO and SEO in one platform Custom; 3-week free trial AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity (via official APIs) How much do AI visibility tools cost? AI visibility tools cost from $0 to about $300 per month on entry plans, and enterprise plans are custom. A fairer comparison is the price per tracked prompt on the entry plan, at the monthly price unless a plan is sold yearly only: Tool (entry plan) Price per month Prompts Cost per prompt Refresh SE Visible Basic $99 200 $0.50 Not stated ZipTie Starter preset $25.65 30 $0.86 Daily LLM Pulse Starter €49 50 €0.98 Weekly Peec AI Starter €85 50 €1.70 Daily Surfer AI Search Analytics $95 50 $1.90 Daily Promptwatch Essential $95 50 $1.90 Daily Otterly.AI Lite $29 15 $1.93 Not stated Writesonic Starter $99 50 $1.98 Daily Scrunch Core $250 125 $2.00 Every 72 hours after 14 days Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit $99 25 $3.96 Daily Cost per prompt is only part of the picture: check how many engines each plan includes, how often data refreshes and whether answers come from real interfaces. ZipTie's preset covers three engines and SE Visible's four, while Surfer's covers five. Yearly billing lowers most of these: Surfer to $1.64 per prompt, Peec AI to €1.40, Otterly.AI to $1.67, Writesonic and Promptwatch to $1.58, and SE Visible to $0.40. Tools priced in credits (AthenaHQ, Rankscale) or custom (Profound) aren't directly comparable. How do you track AI visibility in Surfer? In Surfer, you add your domain and topics, let it suggest the prompts your buyers ask, and then track your mention rate, position and cited sources daily across five AI engines. Here's the setup, step by step: How to do it in Surfer Track and improve your AI visibility Add your brand. Enter your domain and focus topics. Surfer suggests prompts your customers are likely to ask AI assistants; add or edit your own. Pick competitors. Surfer tracks your visibility score, mention rate and average position next to theirs, daily in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode (on AI Search Analytics, Pro and Peace of Mind). Read the answers. Open any prompt in the AI Tracker tab to see the brands named, the sources cited and the fan-out queries behind the answer. Find the gaps. The Mention Gap report lists sources that cite your competitors but not you: pages to pitch or to outdo. Fix the content. Open the page in the Content Editor (Standard and up) and cover the facts AI answers include for the topic. Start tracking for free or get a free AI visibility audit How do you improve your AI visibility once you track it? You improve AI visibility by winning the prompts you lose: make your pages easy to cite, earn mentions on the sources AI already trusts, and keep ranking in search. These steps move the numbers: Fix the prompts you lose. For each prompt where competitors appear and you don't, check which sources AI cites and whether you have a page that answers the question directly. Make pages easy to cite. Answer the question in the first sentences of each section and cover the topic's key facts. Our guide on how to get cited by AI covers this step by step. Earn mentions on cited sources. Pitch the listicles, reviews and communities that AI already cites; this is digital PR with a target list. See our guide to LLM optimization . Keep ranking in search. AI engines retrieve from search indexes, so traditional SEO still drives AI search visibility. Read more about generative engine optimization . Measure AI traffic. Pair your AI visibility tool with Google Analytics and Google Search Console to see whether visibility turns into visits. How do you choose the right AI visibility tool? Choose the AI visibility tool that covers your buyers' AI platforms, shows citations as well as mentions, and fits your prompt count and budget. Use these five questions to narrow your shortlist: Which AI platforms does your audience use? Most tools cover ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI features. If you need Claude, Copilot or Meta AI, check plan details: they're often add-ons or enterprise-only. Does it read real AI answers? Tools that collect answers from the interfaces people use reflect what buyers see more closely than API results. Does it show citations, not just mentions? Source data tells you which pages to improve and which sites to pitch. Can your team act on the data? Prompt-level detail, competitor visibility and recommendations matter more than a single visibility score. Does the price fit your prompt count? Compare cost per tracked prompt, refresh frequency and how many engines are included. Then test your top two on the same prompts for a couple of weeks. AI answers vary between runs, so look at trends, not single results. Comparing Surfer with a specific tool? Our comparison pages put Surfer side by side with Profound, Peec AI, Semrush, Ahrefs and other SEO and AI visibility tools. Frequently asked questions What are AI visibility tools? AI visibility tools track how often your brand, website or product appears in AI generated answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode. They show the prompts that trigger mentions, your position in AI responses, the sources AI cites and how competitors compare. What is the best AI visibility tool? It depends on your needs. Surfer is best for tracking and improving visibility in one tool, Profound for enterprise depth, Peec AI for flexible team tracking, and Semrush or Ahrefs if you already use their SEO platforms. Otterly.AI, ZipTie and Rankscale are among the cheapest paid options. Are AI visibility tools the same as GEO tools and LLM trackers? Mostly, yes. "AI visibility tool," "AI search visibility tool," "AI brand visibility tool," "LLM tracking tool" and "GEO tool" usually describe the same software: it runs prompts in AI engines and reports mentions, citations and sentiment. Some GEO tools also help you optimize content, which is what Surfer, Writesonic and AthenaHQ add on top of tracking. Can I check my AI visibility for free? Yes. Amplitude's AI Visibility tool and AthenaHQ's Essential plan are free, Ahrefs has a free AI Visibility Checker and HubSpot a free AI Search Grader, and Surfer offers a free AI visibility audit . Surfer, Profound, Peec AI, Otterly.AI, Scrunch, ZipTie, Rankscale and SE Visible offer free starts or trials. Why do AI visibility tools show different results for the same prompts? AI answers change between runs, engines, locations and over time, and tools collect them differently: some read the real interfaces, others use APIs. Track a set of prompts over weeks and compare trends rather than single answers. Do AI visibility tools track traffic from ChatGPT and Perplexity? Some do. SE Ranking connects to GA4, Similarweb reports AI referral traffic, and Profound, Writesonic and Promptwatch show how AI agents and crawlers access your site. You can also track AI referral traffic in Google Analytics with a filter for AI sources.

text: Best AI Search Monitoring Tools for Marketers in 2026 Brands are losing visibility they don’t even know is gone. Their traditional rankings look fine in Search Console, but in the AI-generated answers where buying decisions now happen — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews — they simply don’t appear. That gap is what AI search monitoring tools are built to close.
